email.body1:
Amanda, saw Schoox introduced the AI-powered Learning Impact Suite and won the 2026 Lighthouse Tech Award.

New product momentum usually means more in-market accounts in play than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Schoox off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Amanda, quick follow-up for Schoox.

A new suite launch tends to lift pipeline expectations faster than headcount can follow, and enablement feels that gap first when reps can't get enough qualified meetings. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number, so the gap shows up late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Schoox needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Amanda, last bit of proof for Schoox.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Schoox's reply rate likely compares to other B2B SaaS teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Amanda, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing matters, and a new suite launch keeps an enablement team busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to Schoox either way.
